Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached a short proposal (redwood_proposal_v2.pdf) that outlines a conversion from your current annual contract to a three-year staircase arrangement with quarterly true-ups. High level:

- Year 1: conservative onramp (50% of projected run-rate) to reduce immediate spend impact
- Year 2: step-up to 85% of target run-rate
- Year 3: full committed capacity with optional burst pool
- Quarterly true-up: aligns billing to actual usage, reduces blind spots and keeps cost predictability

Key asks from your side: co-term preference and whether procurement requires PO-based invoicing or DocuSign counter-signature. You mentioned your current agreement ends on 2027-11-15 — if you prefer a co-term, we can align the first true-up to that date and pro-rate the initial period.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up on Thursday 9/2 or Friday 9/3 to walk through the numbers? I included Karthik to run through pricing scenarios and Camila for onboarding/implementation sequencing.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping this simple for your ops team.

Best,
Grace

Hi Grace —

Thanks for sending this through. A few quick items from our side:

1) Co-term: we are strongly inclined to co-term with our existing enterprise agreement that ends 2027-11-15. That keeps our finance closeout simpler.
2) Procurement: we typically need a PO and finance prefers quarterly invoices that map to actual usage after a true-up rather than large prepayments.
3) Legal: we need a short auto-renew clause option (30-day notice to opt-out) — our counsel is okay with an opt-in auto-renew if the language is clear.

A couple of questions for you and Karthik:
- Can you model a scenario where Year 1 is 40% (instead of 50%) of target with an option to accelerate to 70% after the first true-up?
- For the pro-rate to co-term: can you show the invoice impact if the contract starts 10/01/2027 and co-terms to 11/15/2027 (we want to avoid double-billing periods).

Happy to take a call Friday morning if that works for your team.

Best,
Alyssa Grant
